MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ADJOURNED MEETING
  JANUARY 17, 2023

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 7:02 p.m. at City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chambers,
  4045 Palos Verdes Dr. N., Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR CIAROLLA.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR CIAROLLA led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Pope, Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, and Retz

  Commissioners Absent:  Persichina and Romanelli

  City Staff Present:  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  DECEMBER 19, 2022

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR BAIN to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  DECEMBER 19, 2022.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PROPOSED NAMES FOR FUTURE PARK SITE LOCATED AT THE
  NORTHEAST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
January 17, 2023
   Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  COMMISSIONER POPE suggested the names of Triangle Park, Gateway Park,
  Hopkins Park based on location and size of the proposed park.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK suggested the names of Gateway Park, Hillview
  Park, and Pepper Tree Park.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ suggested the names of Tongva Park, Gateway Park,
  Peacock Park.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN suggested the names of Peacock Park and Pepper Tree Park.

  CHAIR CIAROLLA suggested the name of Hopkins Park as he was one of the
  founding fathers of the City. A community member in the audience shared why he
  suggested the name of Hopkins Park in the community survey, in response to VICE
  CHAIR BAIN.

  CHAIR CIAROLLA suggested to condense the list of names and prioritize the
  names at the next meeting. COMMISSIONER POPE concurred with CHAIR
  CIAROLLA’s suggestion.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by CHAIR CIAROLLA to:

  CONDENSE THE SUGGESTED PARK NAMES TO TONGVA PARK,
  TRIANGLE PARK, HOPKINS PARK, PEACOCK PARK, GATEWAY PARK,
  PEPPER TREE PARK, AND HILLVIEW PARK AS THE NAMES TO
  CONSIDER TO PRIORTIZE AT THE NEXT PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  MEETING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  B.  STREET ENTRYWAY BEAUTIFICATION PROGRAM FUNDING REQUEST
  FROM STRAWBERRY LANE

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith explained that the HOA requested $1,750
  in matching funds from the City’s beautification program noting that the HOA would
  pay the costs upfront and the City would then reimburse half of the cost of the
  project, the $1,750 recommended, in response to COMMISSIONER RETZ.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
January 17, 2023
   COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE STRAWBERRY LANES HOMEOWNER ASSOCIATION’S
  REQUEST OF $1,750 IN MATCHING FUNDS FROM THE CITY’S
  ENTRYWAY BEAUTIFICATION PROGRAM FY 22-23.

  AYES:  Pope, Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick and Retz
  ABSENT:  Persichina and Romanelli

  C.  STREET ENTRYWAY BEAUTIFICATION PROGRAM FUNDING REQUEST
  FROM DAPPLEGRAY LANE

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material). He also noted that the Dapplegray Lanes Property Owners Association
  (DLPOA) may be going out for some more bids but recommended approving the
  amount in the report as anything else received by the (DLPOA) would be at a lower
  cost than presented in the report.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ recused himself from any vote as he is a resident of the
  neighborhood.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK also recused himself from any vote as he is also
  a resident of the neighborhood.

  CHAIR CIAROLLA noted that this would not leave them with a quorum and that this
  item would need to be tabled to the next meeting but allowed questions to be asked.

  COMMISIONER RETZ since recused from the vote explained that the entrance
  from Dapplegray covers more land than the entryway to Strawberry Lane thus due
  to the extra square footage would require more money to make the improvements,
  in response to VICE CHAIR BAIN.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ since recused from the vote stated that there are 169
  residents in the Dapplegray neighborhood and that Strawberry Lane is a smaller
  neighborhood on one street and estimates 50 residents, in response to CHAIR
  CIAROLLA and VICE CHAIR BAIN.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ since recused from the vote explained that dues to the
  DLPOA is voluntary and that there are no special assessments. He also explained
  that there is enough money to cover the proposed $9,205 cost, in response to VICE
  CHAIR BAIN.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
January 17, 2023
   Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted that the item would be tabled to
  the next meeting due to no longer having a quorum for the item.

  D.  ROCKBLUFF PARK UPDATE

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas confirmed that this project would require
  a current year budget adjustment in the amount of $10,050, which incorporates
  approximately a 10% contingency ($4,560) as written in the report, in response to
  COMMISSIONER RETZ. She added that it was recommended to be received and
  filed as the item would be submitted to City Council at their next meeting for
  approval, in response to COMMISSIONER RETZ.

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith stated that he presented the report to
  continue to keep the Commission informed regarding the status of the playground
  at Rockbluff Park since they were such an integral part in the process from the
  beginning.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN inquired about the cost of the project and if it entailed any
  additional costs from what was budgeted for the project. Maintenance
  Superintendent Goldsmith explained that there were no additional costs to this
  project.

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas explained that the initial installation of the
  ADA ramp did not meet proper ADA specifications and that the City would have an
  ADA consultant involved for future ADA project installations, adding that the City
  went with the specifications from the contractor. Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith also noted that the initial ramp error did not cause any additional costs
  as the $45,490 would have been part of the initial project. He also stated that the
  handrails are a custom build due to the design of the ramp and that a competitive
  bid process was completed, in response to VICE CHAIR BAIN.

  E.  2023 COMMITTEE/SUBCOMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS

  Community Services Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the proposed
  Commissioner committee, subcommittee, and adopt-a-park assignments for the
  upcoming year (2023). He noted the preferences of Commissioner Persichina who
  was absent from the meeting. He also noted that a final copy of the Commissioner
  assignments would be included in an upcoming Park and Activities (P&A) weekly
  update.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
January 17, 2023
   COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK requested to be part of the City Celebration
  subcommittee. COMMISSIONER RETZ agreed to withdraw his name from that
  subcommittee.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN requested to remain on her current committees and adopt-a-
  park assignments.

  COMMISSIONER POPE requested to switch with COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA
  for the Hills Are Alive subcommittee and he could take her spot on the Tracy Austin
  Tennis Tournament subcommittee.

  Community Services Coordinator Morrow stated that he had not heard anything
  from COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI regarding his assignments, in response to
  CHAIR CIAROLLA.

  CHAIR CIAROLLA stated that this would most likely be her last year serving as the
  P&A representative on the Equestrian Committee.

  F.  2023 COUNCIL MEETING ATTENDANCE SCHEDULE

  Community Services Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the proposed
  Commissioner City Council meeting attendance schedule for the upcoming year
  (2023). He noted a recommendation from last year to pre-assign meetings for the
  Commissioners to attend on a rotating basis. COMMISSIONER RETZ volunteered
  to be the P&A representative at the first City Council meeting being held on January
  24, 2023. Community Services Coordinator Morrow also noted that he would
  include the final copy of the meeting attendance schedule and confirm that City
  Council meetings would no longer be hybrid for the upcoming year (2023) in the
  next P&A weekly update.

  CHAIR CIAROLLA made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR BAIN, to adjourn to
  the Pepper Tree Foundation Advisory Board meeting.

  **ADJOURN TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD MEETING**

  G.  ADVISORY BOARD REVIEW OF PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ANNUAL
  REPORT

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  CHAIR BAIN inquired about the Other Uses & Interest category in the Pepper Tree
  Fund Balance Report. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas explained that any
  funds that do not fall into the other categories fall into the Other Uses & Interest

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
January 17, 2023
   category. She also explained that she would inquire about the Other Uses & Interest
  ending balance number to provide an explanation at a later date, in response to
  CHAIR BAIN.

  CHAIR BAIN inquired about how the advisory board could request different or new
  events to support the Pepper Tree Fund. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas
  explained that she would look into that and provide that information at a later date.

  BOARD MEMBER RETZ moved, seconded by BOARD MEMBER POPE, to
  reconvene the Parks and Activities Commission Meeting.

  **RECONVENE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING**

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  FEBRUARY MEETING DATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted that the standard third Monday of
  the month in February (February 20) fell on Presidents Day and wanted to see if
  the Commission would like to consider adjourning to a Tuesday, February 21 date
  for the meeting in February.

  The Commission affirmed and agreed that Tuesday, February 21 would be best for
  the February meeting.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  VICE CHAIR BAIN reported that Highridge Park has a lot of erosion on the trails
  and the area near the turf removal is still puddling. Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith noted that due to the surface material of the trail it is a consistent issue
  and that his crew would look at the trails and attend to them where necessary and
  investigate the puddling.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN inquired about the amount and size of the boulders and rocks
  for the turf removal project as well as if benches would be installed as it would make
  the area more aesthetically pleasing. She also asked if staff were satisfied with the
  result of the project and commended the crew. Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith responded that staff were satisfied with how the turf removal project
  turned out and that the boulders and rocks came from different areas of the City
  and the surrounding areas of the South Bay. He also noted that some fencing
  needed to be replaced which should help make the area look better as the fencing
  was removed to install some of the rocks.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
January 17, 2023
   B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK made a request about the perimeter fencing
  selected with the development of the new park. He requested a green chain link
  perimeter fence be installed around the busy street intersection of PV Drive N and
  PV Drive E as he felt it would assist in deterring children from possibly entering
  those high traffic areas around the park, if there were funds available.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF DECEMBER 13, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  PARK CAMERAS

  B.  EVENTS AND ACTIVITIES AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK

  C.  SPORT FIELD USAGE AGREEMENT

  D.  PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER RESTROOMS

  11.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR CIAROLLA MOVED TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:59 PM TO THE NEXT PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION MEETING ON FEBRUARY 21, 2023, AT 7:00 P.M., WHICH WILL
  BE HELD AT THE CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBER.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________
  Matt Morrow  Valerie Ciarolla
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
January 17, 2023
